summary: On Shionoya (1878–1962) was a sinologist. He studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1903–1906) and Leipzig University (~1912–1915), and later held a post at Tokyo Imperial University (~1920–1939).
Orgyen Jikdral Chöying Dorjé studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He also taught Shechen Gyaltsab.
Orgyen Tendzin Norbu studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He later taught Khenpo Shenga.

Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar Orna Almogi studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute, under Khenpo Wangchuk Sonam (1995), and under doctoral supervisors David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen. She held posts at the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project and University of Hamburg (attested 2007).

Osamu Hayashima is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Noritoshi Aramaki and at the University of Hamburg (1992). He held professorships at Nagasaki University (attested 1979–2003), Shiga University of Medical Science (attested 2003–2013), and Ryukoku University (attested 2013–2015).
Osamu Izumoji (born 1948) works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held academic posts at Kyoto Prefectural University and Ryukoku University.

Osamu Takata (1907–1991) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Baiei Henmi and served as head of the art department at the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties.

Osborn Bergin (1873–1950) was a linguist who studied at University College Cork, under Kuno Meyer at the School of Irish Learning, and under Heinrich Zimmer at the University of Freiburg. He held posts at University College Dublin and the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies.

Oskar von Hinüber is an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Paul Thieme and at Mainz, Tübingen, and Erlangen-Nürnberg. He held posts at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz, the Nepal Research Centre, and a professorship at the University of Freiburg (1981–2006).

Osmund Bopearachchi specializes in history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Kelaniya, CNRS, and Paris-Sorbonne institutions under Paul Bernard and Jean-Marie Dentzer, later serving at CNRS and the University of California, Berkeley.

Osvald Sirén (1879–1966) was a scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology who earned his doctorate at the University of Helsinki. He held positions at Stockholm University (1908–1923), Harvard, Yale, the Musée Guimet, and the Nationalmuseum (1926–1945).

Indologist Othmar Frank (1770–1840) studied at the Universities of Paris (~1814–1816) and London (~1817–1819). He taught at Banz Abbey School and Kaiser-Heinrich-Gymnasium Bamberg, and held professorships at the Universities of Bamberg, Würzburg, and Munich.
Otoya Tanaka (1903–1989) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1925–1928) under Naoshiro Tsuji. He later held a professorship at Chuo University (~1962–1974).

Otto Blau (1828–1879) worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under August Friedrich Pott at the University of Halle (~1848–1850) and also studied at Leipzig University (~1850–1852).

Otto Fischer (1886–1948) was an art historian in sinology and Japanology who studied at Tübingen, Munich, Vienna, and Göttingen. He served as director at Staatsgalerie Stuttgart and Kunstmuseum Basel, and was an extraordinary professor at the University of Basel (~1927–1937).

Otto Franke (1863–1946) was a scholar of sinology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Freiburg, Göttingen, and under Wilhelm Grube. He held the chair of Chinese Language and Culture at the Hamburg Colonial Institute/University of Hamburg and was later professor at Humboldt University.

Otto Höfler (1901–1987) was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies who studied under Rudolf Much and at the Universities of Vienna, Lund, and Kiel. He held professorships at the Universities of Kiel, Munich, and Vienna.

Otto Jahn (1813–1869) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. After studying at Kiel, Leipzig, and Humboldt University of Berlin, he held academic posts at the universities of Kiel, Greifswald, Leipzig, and Bonn (~1855–1869).

Otto Maenchen-Helfen (1894–1969) worked in sinology, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Vienna, Gothenburg, and Leipzig under August Conrady, and later held posts at the Marx-Engels-Lenin Institute, Mills College, and UC Berkeley.

Otto Neugebauer (1899–1990) was a historian of mathematics and archaeology who studied under Boris Turayev and at Graz, Munich, and Göttingen. He held posts at Göttingen, Copenhagen, Brown University, and the Institute for Advanced Study.
